title: What shapes can two same triangles make?
description: Two cardboard triangles with sides eight, eight and six centimetres are joined in different ways. Reading the outer sides in order names a rhombus, a parallelogram or a kite, and two equal-sided triangles make a rhombus. Keeko doubts that the same triangle always gives the same shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: the order of the outer sides, read going round the shape, gives its name. Watch for students who think two copies of one triangle always make one shape.

source: Take two cardboard cutouts of an isosceles triangle with sidelengths 8 cm, 8 cm, and 6 cm. What are the different ways they can be joined to get a quadrilateral? What quadrilaterals are these? Justify your answers.
video_script.why: The child sees that the way two copies of a triangle are joined changes the order of the outer sides, and so the name of the shape.
video_script.substitution: the book's own cutouts of the triangle with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm, and of the 8 cm equilateral triangle
video_script.anchor: two cardboard triangles with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm joined along a side
video_script.wrong_answer: the same triangle always makes the same shape
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks two copies of the same triangle can only make one shape, but flipping a copy changes the order of the outer sides.
video_script.payoff_line: We get a rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite

final_answer.value: A rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite; two equilateral triangles give a rhombus
final_answer.spoken: a rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite, and two equilateral triangles give a rhombus

hold_back: A rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite; two equilateral triangles give a rhombus
never_show: the kite written as a parallelogram
maths_rules: joined along the 6 cm side, the four outer sides are 8, 8, 8 and 8 cm, so it is a rhombus
joined along an 8 cm side with one copy turned half round, the outer sides are 8, 6, 8 and 6 cm, so opposite sides are equal and it is a parallelogram
joined along an 8 cm side with one copy flipped over, the outer sides are 8, 8, 6 and 6 cm in order, so two pairs of neighbouring sides are equal and it is a kite
two equilateral triangles of 8 cm joined along a side have four sides of 8 cm, so it is a rhombus
video_script.design: One idea: read the outer sides in order and match them to a family. Two triangles are drawn on the board and slid into each joining in turn.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two cardboard triangles with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm lying side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is an activity from your book with cardboard triangles.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Two same triangles have sides of eight, eight and six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We join them along a side to make a four-sided shape.
How many different shapes can we make?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a four-sided shape with its outer sides read in order going round, shown as a list of lengths

marks.read: the outer sides are read in order going round the shape
marks.list: the lengths appear as a list

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>To name a four-sided shape, we read its outer sides in order going round.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The joined side is inside, so we do not count it.

beats.on_screen: Given: two copies of a triangle with sides 8 cm, 8 cm, 6 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two copies of a triangle with sides eight, eight and six centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the shapes made by joining the copies in different ways
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to name the shapes we can make.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: join along the 6 cm side; outer sides 8, 8, 8, 8, so a rhombus

marks.join: the two triangles are joined along the six centimetre side
marks.sides: the four outer sides light up with eight centimetres each

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step one, join the copies along the six centimetre side.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The four outer sides are all eight centimetres.
A shape with four equal sides is a rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: join along an 8 cm side, one copy turned half round; outer sides 8, 6, 8, 6, so a parallelogram

marks.turn: one copy turns half round and joins along an eight centimetre side
marks.sides: the outer sides light up as eight, six, eight and six

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, join along an eight centimetre side, with one copy turned half round.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The outer sides are eight, six, eight and six.
Opposite sides are equal, so it is a parallelogram.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: join along an 8 cm side, one copy flipped over; outer sides 8, 8, 6, 6, so a kite

marks.flip: one copy flips over and joins along the eight centimetre side
marks.sides: the two eight centimetre sides and the two six centimetre sides light up as neighbours

narration: <bookmark mark='flip'/>Step three, join along an eight centimetre side, with one copy flipped over.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>Two neighbouring sides are eight centimetres, and the other two are six.
A shape with two pairs of equal neighbouring sides is called a kite.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: two equilateral triangles of 8 cm joined along a side; outer sides 8, 8, 8, 8, so a rhombus

marks.eq: two equilateral triangles are joined along a side
marks.sides: the four outer sides light up with eight centimetres each

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step four, join two equilateral triangles of eight centimetres along a side.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The four outer sides are all eight centimetres, so it is a rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite; two equilateral triangles give a rhombus
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>We get a rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite.
Two equilateral triangles give a rhombus.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: the same two triangles appear once
marks.flip: one copy flips over and the outer sides change order

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the same triangle always makes the same shape.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>But flip one copy over, and the order of the outer sides changes.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A new order of sides can mean a new name, so we must try every joining.
